title: WebMacro
subtitle: Share SQL macros through a trusted URL.
intro: Load a DuckDB macro definition from an HTTPS endpoint and call it in ordinary SQL. Use reviewed, versioned SQL files to distribute reusable scalar expressions and table queries across notebooks and applications.

reference.name: load_macro_from_url(url)
reference.description: Fetch over HTTPS and register one macro; return a status string.

reference.name: CREATE MACRO name(args) AS expression
reference.description: Define a scalar macro in the hosted SQL file.

reference.name: CREATE MACRO name(args) AS TABLE …
reference.description: Define a table macro called from a FROM clause.

reference.name: CREATE OR REPLACE MACRO …
reference.description: Let reloading replace a previously registered definition.

reference.name: SET webmacro_allow_http = true
reference.description: Permit plain http:// URLs, refused by default; trusted networks only.

reference.name: SET webmacro_max_response_size = n
reference.description: Largest accepted response in bytes; the default is 1 MiB.

reference.name: DROP MACRO name
reference.description: Remove a loaded macro with DuckDB's ordinary lifecycle command.

notes.title: The SQL file is executable code
notes.body: Load only reviewed SQL from a trusted host. The response must hold exactly one CREATE MACRO statement, but that check is not a sandbox. Pin immutable revision URLs when reproducibility matters; a branch URL can change after review.

notes.title: Load dependencies first
notes.body: Each call fetches its URL again through DuckDB's HTTP stack: http_timeout, http_proxy and HTTP secrets apply, and redirects are rechecked. There is no dependency resolver, so load prerequisite macros first. Nothing is fetched while enable_external_access is false.

examples.title: Prepare a reusable definition
examples.caption: Test locally, then publish the CREATE statement as normalize_tag.sql on your host.

examples.title: Load the hosted SQL
examples.caption: Replace the placeholder URL with the trusted SQL file prepared above.
examples.reason: Requires a trusted hosted SQL macro and fetches executable SQL from it.

examples.title: Inspect and remove a macro
examples.caption: After creation or loading, it behaves like an ordinary DuckDB macro.

assertions: CREATE OR REPLACE MACRO normalize_tag(s) AS lower(trim(s)); SELECT CASE WHEN normalize_tag('  Farm  ') = 'farm' THEN true ELSE error('Macro normalization failed') END; DROP MACRO normalize_tag;
